requirement_paraphrase: Remote pilot in command must report to FAA within 10 calendar days operations causing serious injury/loss of consciousness or property damage over $500.
applies_to: US small UAS operators under Part 107

status_note: Cornell LII copy; currency date not shown in fetch
requirement_paraphrase: With vision unaided other than corrective lenses, the remote pilot in command, the visual observer (if used) and the person manipulating the controls must be able to see the aircraft throughout flight to know its location, determine attitude/altitude/direction, observe airspace for traffic or hazards, and determine it does not endanger others' life or property; under 107.31(b) this must be exercised by the RPIC and controls person, or by a visual observer.

Operating limits: groundspeed not above 87 knots (100 mph); altitude not above 400 ft AGL unless flown within a 400-foot radius of a structure and not above 400 ft over the structure's uppermost limit; flight visibility from the control station at least 3 statute miles; at least 500 ft below and 2,000 ft horizontally from clouds.

edition_or_version: Amdt. 89-1 (86 FR 4505, 15 Jan 2021 per LII); §89.115 shown 'edition of October 1, 2026'
status_note: In force; operating compliance since 16 Sep 2023 per federal-regs.com page
requirement_paraphrase: Aircraft must comply with standard remote ID (89.110) or alternative remote ID (89.115): a remote ID broadcast module broadcasting 89.315 message elements from takeoff to shutdown with pilot in sight, land as soon as practicable if broadcast stops, or fly only inside an FAA-recognized identification area.
applies_to: US-registered and foreign civil UAS operating in US

edition_or_version: Guidance (arXiv 2102.01564, 2021); York page: brochure dated Oct 2025
requirement_paraphrase: Six-stage process producing artefacts and a GSN argument per stage: ML safety assurance scoping; ML safety requirements; data management (relevance, completeness, accuracy, balance requirements; dev/test/verification datasets); model learning; model verification (test or formal, independent of development).
applies_to: Autonomous systems with ML components (incl. robots)

requirement_paraphrase: Deployment stage: integrate model, record and monitor development assumptions, monitor inputs against training distribution, log erroneous behaviour, test integration (simulation, HIL, shadow, controlled real-world, with evidence simulator represents reality), and argue an integration claim and an operation claim.

instrument: AMLAS Guidance on Assurance of ML in Autonomous Systems
status_note: Open guidance from University of York
clause_or_section_seen: Six stages: scoping, ML safety requirements, data management, model learning, model verification, deployment
requirement_paraphrase: Process plus GSN argument patterns for ML components; top claim that the ML component meets allocated safety requirements in the defined environment; verification by test and/or formal methods using independent verification data.
applies_to: ML components (mainly offline supervised) in autonomous systems

instrument: AMLAS Guidance on Assurance of ML in Autonomous Systems
requirement_paraphrase: Data requirements must be justified (data requirements justification report) and datasets checked for relevance, completeness, accuracy and balance; environment description must be explicit.

instrument: ANSI/CAN/UL 3300 Service, Communication, Information, Education and Entertainment robots
edition_or_version: Listed as ANSI/CAN/UL 3300:2025 with publish date 2024-05-13
requirement_paraphrase: Adds safety requirements for robots used by or near general consumers, 'where applicable' covering indoor and outdoor locations; catalogue text does not mention temperature or dust.

status_note: Listed as current; part of an ASAM pilot for a new process
requirement_paraphrase: Provides a UML data model and exchange formats (e.g. YAML, OpenSCENARIO DSL) for describing operational, current and target operational domains of ADS.

instrument: Abu Dhabi ITC / SASC autonomous vehicle permits (official release)
status_note: Descriptive release, not a regulation text
requirement_paraphrase: ITC granted first two operating permits for commercial driverless L4 vehicles after safety and operational readiness requirements and testing of performance, sensors and responses in real traffic; supervised by the Smart and Autonomous Systems Council with RegLab and a Ministry of Interior-chaired testing committee; ITC platform logs incidents and violations.

instrument: Adee et al. - Discovery of Perception Performance Limiting Triggering Conditions
requirement_paraphrase: Proposes a Bayesian-network method to find perception triggering conditions; states SOTIF gives no concrete method for identifying new triggering conditions.

instrument: BSI PAS 1883 ODD taxonomy for an ADS
status_note: Publicly Available Specification, not a British Standard; to be withdrawn when published as a BS; reviewed at <=2-year intervals
requirement_paraphrase: Gives a minimum hierarchical ODD taxonomy (scenery, environmental conditions, dynamic elements). Environmental attributes include wind, rainfall, snowfall, particulates (incl. airborne dust and sand) and illumination. Excludes test procedures and monitoring requirements for ODD attributes.

instrument: BSI PAS 1883 ODD taxonomy for an ADS
requirement_paraphrase: Temperature is only an optional extra weather attribute, not a defined attribute; glare is mentioned only as a detrimental effect in the illumination text, though sun elevation and position are illumination attributes (cl. 5.3.3); the term GNSS is not used - positioning is covered as Galileo/GLONASS/GPS under connectivity (5.3.4) with signal strength/interference as optional sub-attributes, and loss of positioning signal appears as an interference zone under scenery zones (5.2.2(e)).

instrument: Burton et al., ML safety case in highly automated driving
requirement_paraphrase: Argues ML performance evidence has limits and needs explicit confidence arguments covering training data, test-data sufficiency and whether results reflect the claim; proposes combining several evidence kinds.
applies_to: ML perception in automated driving (transferable idea)
